  <h1 style="font-size: 2.25rem; font-weight: 800; color: #0f172a; margin-bottom: 0.75rem;">The Workbench Labs</h1>
  <p class="wb-lead">
    The workbench is a set of four teaching labs. Each lab walks through one design loop and compares an open-loop suggestion, a single-layer parameter sweep, and a change that crosses an abstraction boundary. The labs are exercises for reasoning about design loops. They are not measurements, and no result on this page should be cited as evidence.
  </p>
  <div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 0.75rem; margin-top: 1.5rem;">

<h2 style="font-size: 1.6rem; font-weight: 700; color: #0f172a; margin-top: 2.5rem;">What the labs compute</h2>
<p style="color: #334155; font-size: 1rem; line-height: 1.65; max-width: 860px;">
  Loops A, C, and D use analytical Python models with an authored scenario for each design style, so their outcomes are set by the lab author rather than produced by a search or a tool. Loop B synthesizes a naive and a carry-save 32-bit accumulator with Yosys onto the SkyWater SKY130 standard cells and checks the two designs against each other in Icarus Verilog on 1,000 random input vectors, where they agree on every vector. That agreement is a simulation check, not a formal equivalence proof. The timing figures in Loop B come from an illustrative per-stage delay model, not from a timing analyzer.
</p>
<p style="color: #334155; font-size: 1rem; line-height: 1.65; max-width: 860px;">
  Earlier versions of this page reported cycle counts, slack, congestion, design-rule counts, and signoff rates as measured results from SCALE-Sim, Yosys, RISC-V GCC, and QEMU. Those numbers were typed into the lab scripts or computed by a fallback formula, so they were removed on 29 September 2026, along with the result figures, screencasts, and exported notebook that displayed them.
</p>

<h2 style="font-size: 1.6rem; font-weight: 700; color: #0f172a; margin-top: 2.5rem;">Run the labs locally</h2>

<div class="docker-box">
# 1. Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/harvard-edge/arch2.git
cd arch2

# 2. Build the workbench container image
./arch2 docker build

# 3. Run an individual lab
./arch2 docker lab 01    # Microarchitecture Sweep
./arch2 docker lab 02    # RTL Timing Closure
./arch2 docker lab 03    # Macro Placement Congestion
./arch2 docker lab 04    # HW/SW Co-Design
</div>
